Covered sugar bowl 
England, ca. 1780 
Earthware (pearlware), 9.9 x 11.7 cm 
Asian Civilisations Museum, 2007-55778 
Gift of Mr and Mrs Tosho Egawa 
Fascinated by the landscapes they saw in Chinese paintings and ceramics, customers in the West wanted European porcelain decorated with similar designs. But for each of the craftsmen who decorated these objects had ever been to China, and their imaginations resulted in landscapes, people and animals that audiences in China would have barely recognised, such as the pagodas and trees depicted with hatched and cross-hatched lines on this bowl. Combining Asian motifs with Western embellishments, the twisted handles with moulded leaf appliqués were inspired by contemporary rococo designs on ceramics and metalware. The bowl is made of pearlware, a greyish earthenware with a blue-tinged glaze made in several English factories as a substitute for Chinese porcelain.
